Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + a few follow-ups so we can tighten the pricing/ops recommendation:

What I heard on the call:
- Monthly token footprint: rough baseline ~800M tokens/month (aggregate), with bursts to ~2.5-3B in peak months.
- Geography: ~70% EU-based traffic (both product and regulated customers), ~30% US.
- Residency requirement: EU inference residency required for EU traffic (no egress of inference data outside EU).
- Target unit economics: you mentioned a target of roughly $200-$250 per 1M tokens as the goal for hosted costs.
- Procurement timeline: aiming for decision by end of Q4; PO & SOW expected in early Nov.

Open items we need from you to finalize a proposal:
1) Confirm whether EU residency must apply to ALL model types (chat/generation + embeddings) or just PII-sensitive endpoints.
2) Expected committed monthly tokens (if you have a floor for a reserved capacity offer).
3) Any regulatory docs we should be aware of (Data Processing Agreement clauses, KMS requirements).

High-level next steps from our side:
- I'll run a short cost comparison (hosted US vs hosted EU vs dedicated/reserved) and share a per-1M-token unit economics sheet.
- We'll include estimates for both raw hosted and committed (12-mo) reserved pricing plus notes on where batching/caching helps reduce cost.
- Sean (cc'd) will outline any procurement/discount levers and typical SLA terms.

I'll follow up in ~2 hours with a compact breakdown. If anything above needs correction, let me know.

Best,

- Residency: EU inference residency is required for all EU-origin requests (chat + embeddings). We can route US traffic to US if that reduces cost.
- Volumes: we can commit to a conservative floor of 500M tokens/mo initially, with projections to reach ~1B within 6 months. Peak months during campaigns may hit 2-3B.

Hi Julia, thanks, great notes. Attached is the compact breakdown (redwood-pricing-1m-token-breakdown.xlsx) - the key numbers are summarized below. These are estimates based on the volumes you shared (500M floor -> 1B projected). We'll refine with a PO/commit.

Summary unit economics (Hosted / Per 1M tokens):
- Hosted (US region): ~$220 per 1M tokens (baseline, pay-as-you-go).
- Hosted (EU region): ~$260 per 1M tokens (baseline, ~18% higher vs US).

Dedicated / Reserved (12-month commitment, recommended if you hit >=500M tokens/mo):
- Dedicated Reserved (US): ~$110 per 1M tokens (with typical 12-mo commit and 50%+ utilization).
- Dedicated Reserved (EU): ~$130 per 1M tokens (EU pricing ~18% premium vs US due to instance and infra costs + KMS integrations).

Notes / assumptions that drive EU delta:
- Instance pricing in EU regions is typically 10-15% higher for GPU families we use; additional overhead for strict data residency routing and region-isolated control plane adds ~3-5%.
- Customer-managed KMS in EU has a slight ops overhead (we include integration & key rotations in the estimate).
- Cross-region egress avoided for EU-resident requests; if you later need cross-region replication for model artifacts, that's additional.

Optimization levers (how you get toward your ~$200/1M target):
- Batching & KV caching: for conversational flows with heavy system prompts, intelligent batching + prefix caching can reduce token costs by 20-40% on average, bringing hosted effective cost closer to $150-$200/1M.
- Quantized model variants: switching to a compatible quantized variant for lower-cost footprints on Dedicated can push reserved unit cost closer to $80-$100/1M (depends on quality tolerance).
- Commitment discounts: with a 12-mo committed volume and a <3-6 month ramp, we typically provide an additional 20-30% off hosted list rates.

Answers to your questions:
1) The EU hosted numbers include expected incremental costs for EU-only hosting + KMS integration; they do not include optional paid replication or cross-region backup.
2) Yes - we can guarantee EU residency for EU-origin requests via region-aware routing and per-route model pins. Consolidated billing and a single contract are standard; we'll surface per-region line items on the invoice.

Next steps I recommend:
- Confirm committed floor (e.g., 500M tokens/mo) so we can lock a reserved proposal vs hosted.
- If you're comfortable, accept the attached term sheet and we'll generate a DocuSign for signature (I'll queue Sean for procurement/discounts).
- 30-min follow-up next week to finalize residency config and timeline.

I've attached: pricing sheet, SOC2 report, and a short mutual action plan (MAP) doc.

Best,
Marissa Cole
